scripts.purpose: Installs every local/*.sh script into /usr/local/bin, deploys remote/*.sh scripts over SSH to configured hosts, and installs the shared config template while migrating a legacy config.conf. Arguments are ignored; settings come from the config file and environment.

environment.name: SUDO_USER
environment.description: Invoking user whose home directory and numeric uid/gid own the deployed config; falls back to the current user.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the user-scripts config directory.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Explicit config supplying remote deployment settings; takes precedence over installed, legacy, and repository configs.

environment.name: REMOTE_SERVERS
environment.description: Array of user@host targets from the config; an empty list disables remote deployment.

environment.name: REMOTE_INSTALL_DIR
environment.description: Destination directory for deployed scripts on each remote host.

environment.name: SSH_TIMEOUT
environment.description: Non-interactive ssh/scp connect timeout in seconds.

write_paths: remote temporary directory created by mktemp -d
network_hosts: each user@host entry in REMOTE_SERVERS (ssh and scp)

exit_codes.meaning: All local scripts were installed (individual local failures are reported only), config was deployed, and every configured remote deployment succeeded; no remote hosts is also success.
Not run as root, an explicitly requested config file is unreadable, or one or more remote deployments failed.

scripts.purpose: Removes the scripts listed in local/ from /usr/local/bin by name, leaving the config and repository files untouched. --dry-run reports intended removals without deleting anything.

arguments.name: --dry-run
arguments.description: Print 'Would uninstall <name>' for each script instead of removing files.

exit_codes.meaning: Help or dry-run output printed, or every removal succeeded; missing installed scripts are not errors.
Not run as root, an unrecognized option was supplied, or an rm command failed.

scripts.purpose: Creates a gzip-compressed tar archive of BACKUP_SOURCES with EXCLUDES and verifies it, optionally sending a desktop notification. --dry-run validates the setup without creating an archive.

arguments.name: -h|--help
arguments.description: Print usage and the option list, then exit 0.

arguments.name: -c|--config-file FILE
arguments.description: Load settings from FILE; takes precedence over USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG and installed/legacy/repository lookup. A missing value exits 2.

arguments.name: --config-file=FILE
arguments.description: Equivalent to -c FILE; an empty value exits 2.

arguments.name: --dry-run
arguments.description: Skip archive creation and verification; report the archive path that would be produced.

arguments.name: --wait-for-notification-daemon
arguments.description: Wait in 60-second intervals until dunst, mako, xfce4-notifyd, or notification-daemon is running.

arguments.name: --notify-send
arguments.description: Send a desktop notification after completion; exits 1 when no notification daemon is running.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Config file path used when no config-file option is given.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the installed config lookup.

environment.name: BACKUP_DIR
environment.description: Destination directory for the archive; created when missing.

environment.name: ARCHIVE_HEADER
environment.description: Filename prefix before the 14-digit timestamp.

exit_codes.meaning: Help printed, dry-run completed, or archive created and verified; a notification is sent when requested.
Config file unreadable, a BACKUP_SOURCES directory missing, archive creation or verification failed, no notification daemon running with --notify-send, or an unknown option supplied.
A config-file option was supplied without a non-empty value.

scripts.purpose: Produces a read-only Arch Linux maintenance report covering updates, caches, services, timers, journals, filesystems, backups, Timeshift snapshots, and Git status, then resets the local maintenance reminder state. It never installs, upgrades, removes, or cleans anything.

arguments.name: -c|--config-file FILE
arguments.description: Load settings from FILE; a missing value exits 2.

arguments.name: --config-file=FILE
arguments.description: Equivalent to -c FILE; an empty value exits 2.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Config file path used when no config-file option is given.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the installed config lookup.

environment.name: BACKUP_DIR
environment.description: Directory searched for fresh backups.

environment.name: ARCHIVE_HEADER
environment.description: Prefix required on backup filenames.

environment.name: MAX_BACKUP_AGE_DAYS
environment.description: Age in days at which the newest backup counts as overdue.

environment.name: MIN_SNAPSHOTS
environment.description: Minimum number of Timeshift snapshots required.

environment.name: MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_DAYS
environment.description: Age in days at which the newest snapshot counts as too old.

environment.name: GIT_CHECKER
environment.description: Executable used for the Git repository check.

environment.name: STATE_DIR
environment.description: Directory holding the maintenance countdown and pending marker.

network_hosts: git remotes of repositories checked by GIT_CHECKER

exit_codes.meaning: Help printed or the report completed; individual checks may print warnings or errors without changing the exit status.
Run as root, pacman missing, or config file unreadable.
A config-file option was supplied without a non-empty value.

scripts.purpose: Notifies when local maintenance is due based on DAYS_DUE and the last-reminder timestamp, repeating while a pending marker exists. Remote checks run only when SERVER is non-empty and SERVER_USER is set.

arguments.name: -c|--config-file FILE
arguments.description: Load settings from FILE; a missing value exits 2.

arguments.name: --config-file=FILE
arguments.description: Equivalent to -c FILE; an empty value exits 2.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Config file path used when no config-file option is given.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the installed config lookup.

environment.name: STATE_DIR
environment.description: Directory holding local countdown and pending state.

environment.name: DAYS_DUE
environment.description: Maintenance interval in days; a non-numeric value warns and falls back to 6.

environment.name: SERVER
environment.description: Remote host for maintenance checks; an empty value disables them.

environment.name: SERVER_USER
environment.description: SSH user for SERVER; an empty value skips remote checks with a warning.

environment.name: SSH_TIMEOUT
environment.description: SSH connect timeout in seconds.

environment.name: REMOTE_STATE_DIR
environment.description: Remote state directory relative to the remote home.

exit_codes.meaning: Help printed or notifications sent/logged; unreachable server, missing notify-send, invalid DAYS_DUE, and missing remote state are warned about rather than failing.
Config file unreadable, or local state directory/timestamp could not be created.
A config-file option was supplied without a non-empty value.

scripts.purpose: Discovers Git repositories under SEARCH_DIR, pruning IGNORE_DIRS and nested .git directories, then reports working-tree changes and ahead/behind status against each branch's upstream, followed by a summary.

arguments.name: -c|--config-file FILE
arguments.description: Load settings from FILE; a missing value exits 2.

arguments.name: --config-file=FILE
arguments.description: Equivalent to -c FILE; an empty value exits 2.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Config file path used when no config-file option is given.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the installed config lookup.

environment.name: SEARCH_DIR
environment.description: Root directory searched for Git repositories.

write_paths: Git refs/FETCH_HEAD under each discovered repository (git fetch --prune)
network_hosts: git remotes configured in discovered repositories

exit_codes.meaning: Help printed or the repository summary completed; dirty, diverged, detached, or upstream-less repositories are counted in the summary but do not fail the script.
A config-file option was supplied without a non-empty value.
